title: Projects of the person's GitLab connections
description: GET /api/v1/integrations/gitlab/repos takes no query. The mapped daemon reads each usable glab login's member projects (GET /projects?membership=true, keyset pagination by id) with that login's own token within a time, page, result and byte bound. Each connection is its own source with its own state: one failing never empties another, and a failed source is never an empty success. Before listing, the token must still authenticate the user glab's entry names (account_mismatch otherwise). complete is true only when the last page carried no next link within the bounds and every page continued the one before; GitLab's next link is checked against the base, never followed. A project whose clone address GitLab gives outside the connected base (a GitLab whose external_url names another address) is never listed, so the token is never sent there: elsewhere counts them. A project is identified by its source's connection_id and GitLab's own numeric id, never by its path alone. Archived projects are listed and marked.

incomplete.description: Why an ok source is not complete: limit (a page, result or byte bound, or the reply's bound across sources, was reached), interrupted (a later page failed or the time bound ran out), inconsistent (the pages disagreed: a repeated or reordered id, a link outside the list, or a project whose path could mean another one).

elsewhere.description: Projects left out because GitLab gives their clone address outside the connected base, and one such address's scheme and server for the person to tell GitLab's administrator.

visibility.description: internal: every signed-in user of that GitLab can see it.

activity_at.description: GitLab's last_activity_at: the last activity of any kind, not a push time.

size_kib.description: GitLab's repository size in KiB; null when GitLab does not tell (it does only to Reporter and above).

empty.description: GitLab says the repository has no commits; such a project cannot be cloned as a workspace yet.

personal.description: The namespace is a user's, not a group's.

own.description: The namespace is the user the token authenticates.
